title: Uniform smooth-support divisors for numerically trivial twists on a nodal curve
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $C/k$ be a nonempty proper connected reduced nodal curve of pure dimension one [def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [def-weil-pure-dimension]. Put $g=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$, with cohomology as in [def-sc-sheaf-cohomology-functor]. For every reduced irreducible component $Z$, let $\nu_Z:\widetilde Z\to C$ be its normalization map [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. For an invertible module $A$ [def-sc-invertible-module], write $\deg_Z(A)=\chi(\widetilde Z,\nu_Z^*A)-\chi(\widetilde Z,\mathcal O_{\widetilde Z})$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], [def-pc-euler-characteristic], [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $H,L$ be invertible modules with $\deg_Z(H)>0$ and $\deg_Z(L)=0$ for every $Z$, and put $h=\sum_Z\deg_Z(H)$. For every integer $m\geq2g+1$ there is an effective Cartier divisor $E$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] on $C$, supported entirely in the smooth locus of $C/k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], such that
$$L\otimes H^{\otimes m}\cong\mathcal O_C(E),\qquad \dim_k\Gamma(E,\mathcal O_E)=mh.$$
Tensor products and powers are those of invertible modules [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The divisor can have multiplicities; no reducedness of $E$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0E3F, lemma-global-generation. The uniform nodal consequence is obtained by the subcurve genus bound and avoidance of finitely many section hyperplanes; its full argument and the existing degree inputs are recorded in report.md. This consequence is not asserted to be the verbatim statement of 0E3F.

proof.text: Put $A=L\otimes H^{\otimes m}$. Since $g$ is a vector-space dimension, $g\geq0$ and $m\geq1$. Tensor products and pullbacks preserve invertibility by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. Apply [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent] to $C$: it is Noetherian and $A,\mathcal O_C$ are coherent. Every closed subscheme $B\subseteq C$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], hence is Noetherian by the same proper-field lemma. In particular its invertible modules and structure sheaf are coherent. Their cohomology is finite-dimensional by [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined].

source.place: Tags 0AYR and 0AYX; proper-coherent finiteness as in coherent.tex Tags 02O5--02O6.

proof.text: Let $B\subseteq C$ be any nonempty reduced connected closed subscheme of dimension one. It is a reduced union of irreducible components of $C$: in a one-dimensional Noetherian space every proper irreducible closed subset of an irreducible component is a closed point; any zero-dimensional component of $B$ would be an isolated open-and-closed point, contrary to connectedness and dimension one. Form $0\to I_B\to\mathcal O_C\to i_*\mathcal O_B\to0$. The ideal is quasi-coherent by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]; on a Noetherian affine its ideal is finitely generated, hence it is coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Thus [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension] gives $H^2(C,I_B)=0$. Apply [lem-sfb-closed-immersion-cokernel-cohomology] to this sequence: $H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)\to H^1(B,\mathcal O_B)$ is surjective, so $g_B:=h^1(B,\mathcal O_B)\leq g$. The same vanishing theorem kills $H^q(B,\mathcal O_B)$ for $q>1$, and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-reduced-algclosed-global-sections-product] gives $H^0(B,\mathcal O_B)=k$. Consequently $\chi(B,\mathcal O_B)=1-g_B$. This includes $B=C$; no smoothness of $B$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0E3F subcurve condition; genus bound from the closed-subscheme cohomology sequence, rather than an uncited dual-graph calculation.

proof.text:
For each reduced irreducible component $Z$, [lem-sc-normalization-properties](a) makes its normalization finite, proper, birational and one-dimensional. Thus [lem-per-birational-curve-degree-invariance] identifies the Euler degree on $Z$ with the degree on its normalization used in the item. Apply [lem-trf-degree-weighted-irreducible-components] on $B$ and on $C$. Since these schemes are reduced, each generic local ring is a field (a reduced local ring with just one prime), so its length over itself is one. Hence for every invertible module $M$ on $C$,
$$\deg_B(M|_B)=\sum_{Z\subseteq B}\deg_Z(M),\qquad \deg_C M=\sum_{Z\subseteq C}\deg_Z(M).$$
These sums are finite. Pullback commutes with tensor products by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. The tensor-degree formula [lem-trf-curve-degree-tensor-additive], iterated $m$ times on the normalized components, gives $\deg_Z(A)=\deg_Z(L)+m\deg_Z(H)=m\deg_Z(H)$. Each positive integer $\deg_Z(H)$ is at least one. Since $B$ contains a component, $\deg_B(A|_B)\geq m\geq2g+1\geq2g_B+1$. Also $\deg_C A=mh$.

Fix any reduced closed point $x\subset C$. Its residue field is $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]. For a reduced closed subcurve $B$, the scheme $x\times_C B$ is either empty or $x$: its ring is the quotient of $k$ by the image of the ideal of $B$, which is either $k$ or zero. Thus its space of functions has dimension at most one. If $H^1(C,I_x\otimes A)\ne0$, apply [lem-sfb-curve-ideal-h1-subcurve-obstruction] to $C,A,x$. It supplies a nonempty reduced connected closed subcurve $B$ with
$$\deg_B(A|_B)\leq -2\chi(B,\mathcal O_B)+\dim_k\Gamma(x\times_C B,\mathcal O)\leq2g_B-1.$$
This contradicts Step 3. Therefore $H^1(C,I_x\otimes A)=0$ for every closed $x$. The obstruction lemma assumes properness, reducedness, connectedness and dimension one, all present; it does not require irreducibility or projectivity.

source.place: Tag 0E3E (lemma-vanishing-on-gorenstein), specialized to the reduced point x; the numerical argument underlying Tag 0E3F.

proof.text: Tensor the ideal sequence of $x$ with $A$. It remains exact by [lem-sc-ext-tensor-exact]. By [lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology] its quotient is $i_*(A|_x)$. The cohomology sequence [lem-sfb-closed-immersion-cokernel-cohomology] and Step 4 now make the evaluation $V:=H^0(C,A)\to A(x)$ surjective. In particular its kernel is a proper $k$-linear subspace for every closed point $x$. By Step 1, $V$ is finite-dimensional. This argument supplies the point evaluations needed below directly, without using any uncited global-generation theorem.

source.place: Tags 0E3E--0E3F, evaluation by the point ideal sequence; cohomology.tex Tag 02UV for closed pushforward.

proof.text: The nonsmooth locus $N$ of $C/k$ is a finite set of closed $k$-points: apply [lem-trf-nodal-marking-special-point-incidence] with the identity extension $k\subseteq k$ and empty marking. Its finite-type, pure-dimension and split-node hypotheses are precisely those of $C$. The components of $C$ are a finite list by Step 3. For each component choose a closed point $q_Z$ on it using [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space]: the closed points of $C$ are dense in every nonempty closed component. Let $T=N\cup\{q_Z\}_Z$, a finite set. The field $k$ is infinite by [lem-sfb-separably-closed-field-infinite], since algebraic closedness implies that every nonconstant separable polynomial has a root. Apply [lem-pc-finite-linear-avoidance] to the kernels of the evaluations $V\to A(x)$ for $x\in T$; they are proper by Step 5. Choose $s\in V$ outside their union. It is nonzero at every node and every $q_Z$, hence its restriction to each component has nonzero generic value: a section of an invertible module on an integral scheme that is zero generically is zero on every affine trivialization, since the affine domain injects into its fraction field, and so is zero at $q_Z$.

source.place: Tags 0C59--0C5B for the finite nodal singular set; finite linear avoidance as in the proof of Tag 0E3F; varieties.tex Tag 0478 for closed points.

proof.text: Let $E=Z(s)$ as in [def-pc-zero-scheme]. On an affine trivialization $A|_U=\mathcal O_Ue$, write $s=ae$. The coordinate ring $R$ is reduced and $a$ is nonzero modulo every minimal prime meeting $U$, by Step 6. If $ab=0$, then in each domain $R/\mathfrak p$ for a minimal prime, $b=0$; hence $b$ belongs to the intersection of the minimal primes, the nilradical, which is zero. Thus $a$ is a nonzerodivisor. Its principal ideal is the local defining ideal of $E$, so $E$ is an effective Cartier divisor by [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. At every point of $N$, the value $s(x)$ is nonzero, so the local coefficient is a unit and $x\notin E$. Therefore $E$ is supported in the smooth locus. This proves regularity on the whole reduced curve, including at nodes, rather than assuming that nonzero sections on a reducible curve are automatically regular.

source.place: Tag 02OQ (definition-zero-scheme-s), local principal-ideal construction; regularity checked directly in a reduced ring.

proof.text:
The section $s:\mathcal O_C\to A$ has Cartier zero scheme by Step 7, so [lem-pc-zero-scheme-divisor-iso] gives $A\cong\mathcal O_C(E)$. The degree-length clause of [lem-pc-degree-base-change], applied on the proper one-dimensional scheme $C$ to the effective Cartier divisor $E$, gives
$$\dim_k\Gamma(E,\mathcal O_E)=\deg_C\mathcal O_C(E)=\deg_C A=mh,$$
where the last equality is Step 3. No assertion that $s$ has simple zeros was made, so multiplicities in $E$ are retained, as required.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0E3E--0E3F: existing ideal-cohomology obstruction gives the required evaluations; agent assembly with the closed-subcurve genus bound, component degrees and finite avoidance.
